name: Kisslinger Kristallglas Rattenberg
kurzbeschreibung: The Kisslinger Kristallglas demonstration glassworks in Rattenberg: centuries-old glassblowing craftsmanship, cutting, engraving, and sparkling glass art.
beschreibung:
Overview

The traditional demonstration glassworks Kisslinger Kristallglas is situated in the medieval centre of Austria's smallest town, the glass city of Rattenberg in the Tyrolean Unterinntal (Kufstein district), at an altitude of around 521 metres. Located right in the historic pedestrian zone at Südtiroler Straße 30, this family-run traditional enterprise epitomises centuries of Tyrolean glassmaking artistry. Across more than 1,000 square metres of exhibition and sales area, visitors experience the entire creation process of exquisite crystal glass – from the glowing furnace to the artfully finished masterpiece.

Glassmaking Art & Demonstration Workshops

The company's roots trace back across several generations. In the glass demonstration workshops, visitors look directly over the shoulders of master glassblowers: at the open melting furnace, the artisans gather the honey-like glass melt heated to over 1,200 °C using a blowpipe and shape it with wooden shaping blocks, shears, and measured lung power into delicate vases, bowls, goblets, and animal figures. Next, guests tour the finishing departments: here, glass cutters and engravers demonstrate traditional cuts and millimetre-precise copper-wheel engravings on rotating diamond wheels. A special highlight is the section dedicated to glass painting and sandblasting techniques. In the spacious crystal gallery, handcrafted chandeliers, fine glassware collections, art objects, and sparkling decorative items gleam brilliantly. For history enthusiasts, a concise historical exhibition illustrates Rattenberg's rise to a world-renowned glassmaking town following the resettlement of Sudeten German glassblowers after the Second World War.

Visit & Getting There

The demonstration glassworks and showroom galleries of Kisslinger Kristallglas are open year-round from Monday to Saturday from 09:00 to 18:00 (Sundays from May to October from 10:00 to 17:00; glassblowing demonstrations run all day Monday to Friday). The admission to the demonstration workshops is free! Guided tours for travel groups are available by advance reservation. Getting there by car: via the Inntalautobahn A12 (exit Kramsach/Brixlegg), take the B171 to Rattenberg; paid parking spaces are available immediately outside the town gates (parking lot Ost or West; the town centre is car-free). By public transport: train (ÖBB/S-Bahn) to Rattenberg-Kramsach station, from where it is just a two-minute walk through the historic town gate directly to the glassworks.

Tips

The demonstration workshops and crystal gallery on the ground floor are barrier-free and fully wheelchair accessible. Adventurous visitors can, by prior reservation and under the expert guidance of the master glassblower, blow their own glass ball to take home as a personal keepsake. Combine your visit with a stroll through the colourful pedestrian zone of Rattenberg or an ascent to the Schlossberg ruins.
